public.prompt: A selection highlight moves between fixed-size tabs while a large dashboard is updating. Profiling shows that animating its `left` and `width` triggers layout and paint across many frames. The effect only needs translation, scaling, and fading. Which policy best reduces rendering work?

options.label: Continue animating `left` and `width`, then add `will-change: all` to every tab for the page lifetime.
Animate `margin-left` and `max-width`, then force synchronous layout before each frame to stabilize geometry.
Measure target geometry outside the frame loop, animate `transform` and `opacity`, and scope `will-change` briefly.

answerProof.summary: Geometry properties such as left, width, margins, and maximum width enter layout and paint work, while transform and opacity can be handled in composition. Measuring once avoids read/write layout churn, and temporary targeted `will-change` avoids persistent layer costs.
decisiveConstraints: The highlight does not need to alter surrounding layout.
Per-frame layout is the measured bottleneck.
Layer hints must not be applied broadly for the page lifetime.

claims.statement: Geometry-affecting properties can trigger style, layout, and paint, while transform and opacity can be handled at the composition stage.
`will-change` should be used sparingly and switched on and off with enough lead time rather than applied broadly.

optionRationales.explanation: The animated geometry still incurs layout work, and broad persistent `will-change` can consume resources without removing that contract.
optionRationales.plausibility: Layer promotion hints can improve some animations and are easy to add without changing coordinates.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The frame path must avoid geometry invalidation and persistent hints across every tab.

optionRationales.explanation: Margins and maximum width also affect geometry, while forced layout inside each frame adds synchronization work.
optionRationales.plausibility: Explicit measurement can prevent visual jumps when an animation depends on changing dimensions.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The effect can be represented without per-frame layout reads or geometry writes.

optionRationales.explanation: It derives endpoints once, keeps frame updates in compositing-friendly properties, and limits promotion hints to active use.
